title: AQ Podcast | Lula’s Comeback and Challenges Ahead
gist: AQ Podcast episode with Folha de S.Paulo's Fábio Zanini on Lula's comeback win by more than four million votes and the challenges ahead: a hostile Congress, nervous markets, a budget deficit approaching 10% of GDP and an uncertain U.S. relationship. The episode asks whether Lula will turn more orthodox economically, bring conservatives into government, and make peace with the Trump administration.

insights.claim: After winning Brazil's 2026 election by more than four million votes, Lula must face a hostile Congress, nervous financial markets and an uncertain relationship with Washington.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
insights.so_what: Frames the main risk factors for Brazilian assets in Lula's fourth term.
insights.locator: After a comeback and a win

insights.claim: Brazil's budget deficit is approaching an unsustainable 10% of GDP.

insights.so_what: Fiscal sustainability is the central macro question for Brazil.

insights.claim: Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula's defeated opponent, has left for the United States, where he is alleging political persecution.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
insights.so_what: Potential source of U.S.-Brazil diplomatic friction.

insights.claim: Over a 40-plus-year career Lula has often evolved according to the needs of the moment, raising the question of whether he will now adopt a more orthodox economic approach.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
insights.so_what: An orthodox pivot would be a positive catalyst for Brazilian markets.
